references.text: Jesus confirms the promise of not tasting death by declaring himself to be the resurrection and the life, and promises that whoever lives and believes in him will live forever even if he dies.
Here Jesus is compared with the bread from heaven that gives eternal life, in contrast to the fathers who ate manna and died, which mirrors the discussion about Abraham and the prophets in John 8.
Jesus promises that whoever hears his word and believes in him has passed from death to life and will not die, which is a direct response to the accusation that he promises impossible eternal life.
Jesus confirms that he gives his sheep eternal life, and that they will never perish, which supports the claim that his words protect against eternal death.
In his prayer to the Father, Jesus refers to the gift of eternal life given through his word and authority, which is the core of the claim in John 8:52.
